overview: Pipa has been part of my life since I was four years old.
pipaIntro: The pipa (琵琶, Chinese plucked lute) is a four-stringed Chinese plucked lute, known for its pear-shaped body, bright attack, and ability to move between lyrical singing lines and intensely percussive storytelling. Its ancestors traveled into China through Central and West Asian musical exchange, and by the Tang dynasty the pipa had become one of the iconic instruments of court and literati music. The repertoire includes poetic pieces such as 春江花月夜 (Moonlit River in Spring), dramatic narrative works such as 十面埋伏 (Ambush from Ten Sides), and beloved modern and regional pieces such as 大浪淘沙 (Great Waves Washing the Sand) and 彝族舞曲 (Dance of the Yi People).
personalNote: I started learning pipa when I was four and received 业余琵琶十级 (Amateur Pipa Level 10) when I was twelve. This portrait was taken while I was playing at Jizushan, 鸡足山 (Jizu Mountain), a Buddhist mountain in Yunnan associated with pilgrimage, monastic practice, and the Mahakasyapa tradition.
